title: The price of an observation
hook: A toy observation has fixed accuracy. How much test cost can its decision value bear?

knows: basic arithmetic and the meaning of a percentage
doesNotKnow: Compare expected decision gain with observation cost under a fully specified toy accuracy and payoff rule.

misconception: An informative observation is worth buying regardless of its cost.
objective: Compare expected decision gain with observation cost under a fully specified toy accuracy and payoff rule.

claims.text: Original stipulated payoff model: A inputs [80, 8, -12] yield 4; B inputs [80, 2, -18] yield -2. Prediction correct option -2. A yields {A}; B {B} over a no-test baseline of zero. Correct decisions gain ten and wrong ones lose ten; increasing the fee subtracts six in both branches. Accuracy and decision payoffs are stipulated; no real measurement’s value is estimated.

claims.text: A toy observation leads to gain 10 with 75% probability and loss 10 otherwise, and always costs 1. Expected net value? Correct and wrong net branches are 9 and −11; 0.75 × 9 + 0.25 × (−11) = 4.
claims.source: Original transfer toy, payoff, inputs [75, 9, -11], output 4; independent Python recomputation.
